children: U.S. job openings rose slightly in July while hiring ticked down, according to a report from the Labor Department's monthly job openings and labor turnover survey.

Available positions rose slightly to 7.3 million in July from 7.2 million in June. Meanwhile, the hiring rate declined to 3.2% in July from 3.4% in June, with about 5.1 million Americans landing new jobs in July.
The number and rate of layoffs and discharges were little changed at 1.7 million and 1%.
The quit rate, or workers leaving their jobs voluntarily, changed little at 3.1 million and 1.9% over the month, the report said.
